next.title: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

title: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

hook.en: Grade 3 is the line between a muscle that can lift the limb and one that cannot. Learn the scale, the gravity-decides rule and how to resist without guessing.
hook.ur: Grade 3 us muscle ke beech ki line hai jo limb ko utha sakta hai aur jo nahi utha sakta. Scale, gravity-decides ka qaida aur bina andaza lagaye resist karna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll grade strength 0–5 for any muscle, choose the correct gravity position, give resistance at the right place and time, and record the result clearly.
goal.ur: End tak aap kisi bhi muscle ki taqat 0–5 grade karenge, sahi gravity position chunenge, sahi jagah aur sahi waqt par resistance denge aur result saaf likhenge.

next.title: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

title: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

hook.en: A weak muscle always borrows help from a stronger neighbour. Learn to spot the shrug, the lean and the swing so a "4/5" really means a 4/5 in the muscle you meant to test.
hook.ur: Kamzor muscle hamesha mazboot padosi se madad leta hai. Shrug, lean aur swing pehchanna seekhein taake “4/5” ka matlab wohi muscle ho jisay aap test karna chahte the.

goal.ur: End tak aap serratus anterior, trapezius, rhomboids, deltoid aur elbow flexors aur extensors sahi test karenge aur har ek ki substitution batayenge.

summaryEn: Every movement has helpers; watch the whole body and use the standard position that blocks the cheat.
Classic cheats: shrug for shoulder lift, trunk lean, wrist flexors for elbow flexion, tenodesis in the hand, winging for serratus anterior.
Watch the scapula, retest in the same position and use a dynamometer for strong muscles; refer for sudden weakness, severe pain or vascular signs.

next.title: MMT of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Gluteals, Quadriceps and the Calf

title: MMT of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Gluteals, Quadriceps and the Calf

hook.en: The legs are the strongest muscles in the body, so the standard hands-on test often says "5/5" when real strength is missing. Learn the correct positions, the Trendelenburg link and why the calf is tested by heel raises.
hook.ur: Taangein jism ke sab se mazboot muscles hain, is liye standard hands-on test aksar “5/5” kehta hai jab asal taqat kam hoti hai. Sahi positions, Trendelenburg ka link aur calf heel raises se kyun test hota hai seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll test gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps and the calf with correct positions and resistance, name the substitution for each and use functional tests for the big muscles.
goal.ur: End tak aap gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps aur calf ko sahi position aur resistance se test karenge, har ek ki substitution batayenge aur bare muscles ke liye functional tests use karenge.

next.title: Muscle Length Testing — Thomas, Ely, Ober, Straight-Leg Raise and the Calf

title: Muscle Length Testing — Thomas, Ely, Ober, Straight-Leg Raise and the Calf

hook.en: "Tight hamstrings" is the most over-used diagnosis in physiotherapy. Learn to test muscle length so carefully that you know which muscle is short, which compensation is hiding it and when stretching is the wrong answer.
hook.ur: “Tight hamstrings” physiotherapy ki sab se zyada istemal hone wali tashkhees hai. Muscle length itni ehtiyat se test karna seekhein ke aap ko pata ho kaun sa muscle chhota hai, kaun si compensation usay chhupa rahi hai aur stretching kab ghalat jawab hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll perform the modified Thomas, Ely, Ober, passive straight-leg raise and gastrocnemius–soleus tests, name the normal finding and the compensation for each, and decide when stretching is justified.
goal.ur: End tak aap modified Thomas, Ely, Ober, passive straight-leg raise aur gastrocnemius–soleus tests karenge, har ek ki normal finding aur compensation batayenge, aur tay karenge ke stretching kab durust hai.

summaryEn: Move passively to the first firm resistance or compensation; two-joint muscles need both joints in position, one-joint muscles need only one.
Know the four tests: Thomas (hip flexors), Ely (rectus femoris), Ober (TFL/ITB), passive SLR (hamstrings), and the calf with the knee straight or bent.
Stretch only if the short muscle matters; separate muscle from nerve with structural differentiation; screen for hypermobility first.

next.title: Limb Length and Girth — True, Apparent and Functional Leg Length, Swelling and Wasting

title: Limb Length and Girth — True, Apparent and Functional Leg Length, Swelling and Wasting

hook.en: A centimetre decides whether a leg is truly short, whether the pelvis is tilted or whether the knee is swollen. Learn tape-measure rules that make every number repeatable.
hook.ur: Ek centimetre tay karta hai ke taang waqai chhoti hai, pelvis tilt hai ya knee sooja hua hai. Tape-measure ke woh usool seekhein jo har number ko repeatable banate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll measure true and apparent leg length, thigh, knee and calf girth and figure-of-eight ankle swelling, and tell structural from functional discrepancy.
goal.ur: End tak aap true aur apparent leg length, thigh, knee aur calf girth aur figure-of-eight ankle swelling naapenge, aur structural ko functional discrepancy se alag karenge.

summaryEn: Five tape habits: mark landmarks, match both sides, tape flat and snug, average two readings, record position and landmarks.
True length (ASIS → medial malleolus) shows structural shortening; apparent length adds pelvic tilt; Galeazzi finds femur versus tibia.
Girth and swelling numbers (thigh, knee, calf, ankle, arm) change management; a calf over 2–3 cm bigger or rapid swelling needs urgent assessment.

next.title: Spinal Mobility and General Measures — Schober, Chest Expansion, Occiput-Wall, Grip and BMI

title: Spinal Mobility and General Measures — Schober, Chest Expansion, Occiput-Wall, Grip and BMI

hook.en: A tape measure can track spinal stiffness, lung expansion and sarcopenia better than the eye. Learn the five simple measures that every clinic should have.
hook.ur: Tape measure rindi spine ki sakhti, phephron ke phailao aur sarcopenia ko aankh se behtar track kar sakti hai. Woh paanch aasan measures seekhein jo har clinic mein hone chahiye.

goal.en: By the end, you'll perform the modified Schober, chest expansion and occiput-to-wall tests, grip strength and BMI/waist measurement and say what each result means.
goal.ur: End tak aap modified Schober, chest expansion aur occiput-to-wall tests, grip strength aur BMI/waist measurement karenge aur batayenge ke har result ka kya matlab hai.

summaryEn: Modified Schober (15 → at least 20 cm), chest expansion (at least 2.5 cm) and occiput-wall (0 cm) track spinal and chest stiffness.
Grip under 27 kg (men) or 16 kg (women) screens for sarcopenia; BMI and waist circumference guide risk and exercise planning.
Standardise every measure (landmarks by palpation, same posture and device) and refer inflammatory or fragile-spine patterns instead of manipulating.

title: Maitland Joint Mobilization

hook.en: Gentle, rhythmic rocking of a joint, graded I to IV by how far into the range you go, chosen by how irritable the patient's pain is.
hook.ur: Maitland Joint Mobilization mein therapist joint ko patient ki taraf se relax halat mein chhoti, narm aur rhythm ke sath aagay-peechay harkat deta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Maitland Joint Mobilization is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)

summaryEn: In one line: Test the movement, choose the glide and grade, test the movement again.
Use it for: A painful, stiff joint where one movement clearly reproduces the patient's pain (positive comparable sign).
Stop or avoid when: Unstable fracture, dislocation, active infection, or suspected cancer in the area.

next.title: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization

title: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization

hook.en: Mobilization that uses joint shape (the convex-concave rule) to pick the glide direction, and traction grades to loosen, take up slack, or stretch.
hook.ur: Kaltenborn–Evjenth approach mein joint par sustained traction ya glide diya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Know the joint shape, choose the glide direction, escalate the stage only if the joint is calm.
Use it for: A joint that moves less than the other side with a firm, capsular-type end-feel.
Stop or avoid when: Unstable joints, acute fractures, active infection or inflammation, and suspected tumour.

next.title: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction

title: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction

hook.en: A gentle pull that separates joint surfaces to reduce compression and test or calm symptoms.
hook.ur: Manual traction ya joint distraction mein joint ko controlled direction mein ahista kheench kar compression-sensitive symptoms ka response dekha jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Manual Traction & Joint Distraction is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Manual Traction & Joint Distraction kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Less pressure, then test: if traction eases the symptom, the joint is involved.
Use it for: Joint pain that eases when compression is removed.
Stop or avoid when: Instability, fracture, infection, or rheumatoid involvement of the upper neck.

next.title: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)

title: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)

hook.en: A sustained joint glide applied by the therapist while the patient performs the movement that normally hurts, aiming for an instant pain-free result.
hook.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) mein therapist ek sustained accessory glide deta hai aur patient usi waqt apni active movement karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Glide, move, ask: if it is not pain-free and instant, it is not the right glide.
Use it for: A clearly painful or restricted movement that is easy to repeat, for example painful gripping at the elbow or restricted ankle dorsiflexion.
Stop or avoid when: No immediate pain-free improvement after a few careful tries.

next.title: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs

title: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs

hook.en: Neck and spine glides applied along the facet joint while the patient moves actively (SNAG) or in gentle oscillation (NAG).
hook.ur: NAGs, SNAGs aur Self-SNAGs spinal mobilization ke tareeqay hain jin mein joint ki glide ko passive ya active movement ke sath combine kiya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Glide along the facet, move the neck, and keep it pain-free.
Use it for: Painful neck rotation or flexion where a segment is tender.
Stop or avoid when: Dizziness, visual disturbance, difficulty speaking or swallowing, or any neurological sign.

next.title: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization

title: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization

hook.en: Hands-on spinal examination: PPIVMs test movement between vertebrae through natural bends; PAIVMs test small glides between them.
hook.ur: PAIVM aur PPIVM spinal assessment ke tareeqay hain: PAIVM mein accessory pressure aur PPIVM mein spine ki physiological movement assess ki jati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Test each level, ask about pain, and prove relevance by retesting.
Use it for: Back or neck pain where you want to find the most relevant segment.
Stop or avoid when: Suspected fracture, instability or serious pathology (use medical assessment first).

next.title: HVLA Thrust Manipulation

title: HVLA Thrust Manipulation

hook.en: A fast, small, controlled thrust at the end of a joint's range, used only after careful screening and supervised training.
hook.ur: HVLA manipulation ek rapid aur chhoti-range thrust hai jo sirf appropriate examination, informed consent aur safety screening ke baad trained clinician perform karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what HVLA Thrust Manipulation is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke HVLA Thrust Manipulation kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Screen, consent, choose the safest effective option, then retest. Never trust the pop.
Use it for: Mechanical back or thoracic pain with local stiffness and no red flags, when the patient agrees and you are trained.
Stop or avoid when: Fracture, osteoporosis, infection, cancer, spinal instability or inflammatory spine disease.

next.title: Neurodynamic Mobilization

title: Neurodynamic Mobilization

hook.en: Gentle movements that slide or lightly tension a nerve so it moves freely and tolerates movement better.
hook.ur: Neurodynamic mobilization mein nervous system aur us ke aas-paas ke tissues ki movement tolerance par kaam kiya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Neurodynamic Mobilization is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Neurodynamic Mobilization kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Slide first, tension later, and never provoke sharp or lingering symptoms.
Use it for: Arm or leg symptoms (tingling, aching, pulling) reproduced by neural tension positions with a clear pattern.
Stop or avoid when: Worsening weakness, spinal cord signs or cauda equina symptoms.

next.title: PNF Manual Techniques

title: PNF Manual Techniques

hook.en: Using the patient's own gentle muscle contractions, with your hand resistance, to improve range, strength and control.
hook.ur: PNF manual techniques mein therapist ki resistance, stretch aur diagonal movement patterns use hotay hain taake coordinated movement aur functional motor control ko facilitate kiya ja sake.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what PNF Manual Techniques is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke PNF Manual Techniques kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Gentle contraction, full relaxation, then move into the new range.
Use it for: Muscle tightness limiting range (hamstrings, calves, shoulder muscles).
Stop or avoid when: Uncontrolled high blood pressure or heart conditions (avoid strong breath-holding).

next.title: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction

title: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction

hook.en: Firm, small rubbing strokes across the fibres of a tendon or ligament, applied exactly on the sore spot.
hook.ur: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction mein symptomatic tendon, ligament ya muscle ke tissue par us ke fibres ki direction ke aar-paar localized pressure aur movement di jati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Find the exact spot, rub across the fibres, then load the tendon.

next.title: Muscle Energy Technique (MET)

title: Muscle Energy Technique (MET)

hook.en: A gentle muscle contraction by the patient against your precise resistance, followed by a stretch or movement into the new range.
hook.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET) mein patient apni muscle se controlled contraction karta hai aur therapist munasib resistance deta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Muscle Energy Technique (MET) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Muscle Energy Technique (MET) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Light push, full relax, then move to the new barrier.
Use it for: Muscle tightness limiting range, for example hamstrings or hip muscles.
Stop or avoid when: Fracture, acute tear, severe osteoporosis or instability.

next.title: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release

title: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release

hook.en: Finding a tender point, then holding the body in the position of most comfort for about 90 seconds to settle it.
hook.ur: Strain Counterstrain ya positional release ek indirect approach hai: sensitive area ko aisi position mein le jaya jata hai jahan patient ko zyada comfort ho, phir dheere se neutral position mein wapas laya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Find the sore point, move toward ease, hold, return slowly.

Stop or avoid when: Unstable fracture or serious joint or spine instability.

next.title: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR)

title: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR)

hook.en: A short, gentle method: find the neutral position of a tight area, add a small compression, then move toward comfort for a few seconds.
hook.ur: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR) ek indirect positional technique hai bodye region ko relative comfort mein rakh kar gentle facilitating force di jati hai.

goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Facilitated Positional Release (FPR) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Neutral, light compression, ease, short hold, retest.

next.title: Myofascial Release (Direct & Indirect)

title: Myofascial Release (Direct & Indirect)

hook.en: Slow, sustained pressure or stretch on the tissue envelope (fascia) until it feels like it softens, either into the restriction (direct) or toward ease (indirect).

goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Myofascial Release (Direct & Indirect) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Slow, steady, follow the tissue, retest.
Use it for: Tight, restricted areas where gentle sustained contact is acceptable.
Stop or avoid when: Open wounds, infection, acute inflammation, or fresh surgery.

next.title: Soft-Tissue Mobilization

title: Soft-Tissue Mobilization

hook.en: Hands-on strokes, kneading and pressure on muscle and soft tissue to relax it, improve circulation and improve movement.

next.title: Trigger-Point Pressure Release

title: Trigger-Point Pressure Release

hook.en: Steady pressure held on a tender knot in a muscle until its pain eases, usually followed by stretching.
hook.ur: Trigger-Point Pressure Release mein muscle ke ek sensitive hissay par ahista, bardasht ke qabil pressure diya jata hai aur symptoms ka response dekha jata hai.
